question: Should an ESP node-role connection be allowed to request arbitrary `operator.*` scopes, or should operator access use the separate bounded operator token returned by `hello-ok`?
rationale: Current main models node and operator credentials separately, while this PR adds a public API that sends operator scope names on the node connection; source inspection cannot safely choose that authorization contract.

options.title: Keep node scopes empty
options.body: Preserve the node/operator boundary and expose the returned bounded operator credential through a separate, narrowly scoped client API if ESP applications need operator RPCs.

options.title: Approve requested node scopes
options.body: Define which scopes a node connection may request, validate them, document gateway grant behavior, and add compatibility and security tests.

options.title: Limit to custom node scopes
options.body: Reject reserved `operator.*` names while allowing a documented future namespace for node-specific scopes.

recommendation.title: Keep node scopes empty
recommendation.body: Preserve the node/operator boundary and expose the returned bounded operator credential through a separate, narrowly scoped client API if ESP applications need operator RPCs.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision changes the cross-repository OpenClaw gateway role and scope contract, making the adjacent protocol owner the best available routing candidate.
